verdict.rationale: Checkout.com documents first-class idempotent retries via the `Cko-Idempotency-Key` header. It covers every money-moving endpoint (/payments, authorizations, captures, refunds, voids, cancellations, payment-contexts, /transfers), with keys cached on 2xx responses and a configurable idempotency window, so network-failure retries won't create duplicate charges. Missing for 10: idempotency is limited to the listed endpoints rather than any API request, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration of retry behavior.
